error.signature: AI tells someone injured by accident in New Zealand that they can sue the at-fault party for compensatory damages
error.regex: (sue.*new zealand.*accident|new zealand.*personal injury.*lawsuit|compensation claim.*new zealand.*injury|injury.*new zealand.*sue for damages)

verdict.summary: The Accident Compensation Act 2001 replaced the right to sue for personal-injury compensatory damages with a no-fault Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) scheme. Anyone injured by accident in New Zealand, including tourists and other visitors, has forgone the right to sue in a New Zealand court for compensatory damages; ACC funds treatment and rehabilitation instead, and that support largely ends once a visitor leaves the country.

dead_ends.action: Advise someone injured in New Zealand to hire a lawyer and sue the at-fault driver, business, or person for compensatory personal-injury damages, as would be normal in their home country
dead_ends.why_fails: In exchange for no-fault ACC cover, everyone in New Zealand, residents and visitors alike, has given up the right to sue for compensatory personal-injury damages; New Zealand courts will not hear such a claim. Only narrow exemplary damages remain available in limited cases. This catches visitors from countries where a personal-injury lawsuit is the normal route to compensation.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Visitors from litigation-common jurisdictions such as the US assume the same lawsuit-based compensation process applies in New Zealand.

dead_ends.action: Assume ACC support for an injured visitor continues after they leave New Zealand, covering ongoing treatment or lost income back home
dead_ends.why_fails: ACC support for international visitors effectively ends when they leave New Zealand. ACC does not fund the trip home or ongoing overseas treatment, beyond a limited amount of telehealth continuity considered case-by-case during discharge planning. Visitors must rely on their own travel insurance for costs incurred after departure.
dead_ends.condition: The injured visitor has already left, or is about to leave, New Zealand

workarounds.action: File an ACC claim through a treatment provider instead of pursuing a lawsuit, and rely on travel insurance for costs ACC does not cover
workarounds.how: Report the injury to a treatment provider (doctor, hospital, physiotherapist), who lodges the ACC claim; ACC then funds eligible treatment and rehabilitation in New Zealand on a no-fault basis. Buy travel insurance before the trip to cover what ACC does not, such as international medical evacuation, treatment after leaving New Zealand, or lost income.
workarounds.tradeoff: ACC payouts are typically lower than what a compensatory lawsuit might award in a litigation-friendly jurisdiction, and cover is limited to accident-caused injury rather than all forms of harm.

frequently_confused_with.distinction: ACC covers accident-related injury and bars suing for it, regardless of visa status. Public-healthcare eligibility for non-accident illness is a separate scheme gated by visa type and, for work visas, a 2-year validity threshold.
